name: COS
description: COS returns the cosine of a given angle. The angle must be expressed in radians.
tldr: Returns the cosine of an angle given in radians.

parameters.name: number
parameters.description: The angle, in radians, for which you want the cosine.

basicExample.explanation: RADIANS(60) converts to π/3; the cosine of π/3 is 0.5.

advancedExamples.title: Cosine of π
advancedExamples.explanation: The cosine of π radians (180°) is -1.

howItWorks: COS computes the cosine of an angle measured in radians. The function is periodic with period 2π, so COS(x) = COS(x + 2πk) for any integer k.

howToSteps.name: Convert if needed
howToSteps.text: If your angle is in degrees, wrap it with RADIANS().

howToSteps.name: Enter the formula
howToSteps.text: Type =COS(number) with the angle in radians.

limitations: The angle must be in radians; degrees must be converted with RADIANS or PI()/180.
Results are approximate due to floating-point math.
COS cannot directly take degrees, unlike some calculator conventions.

commonErrors.cause: Angle was supplied in degrees instead of radians.
commonErrors.fix: Wrap the angle in RADIANS() or multiply by PI()/180.

googleSheetsEquivalent.description: COS works identically in Google Sheets.

faq.question: My COS gives wrong values — why?
faq.answer: Most likely you passed degrees. Convert with RADIANS() first, e.g. =COS(RADIANS(60)).

faq.question: What is the period of COS?
How do I get the inverse (angle from cosine)?
faq.answer: Use ACOS, which returns the angle in radians.
